title: Analytic diagnosis methods for disease ruling
text:
The project targets disease ruling with diagnostic tests, lays out an analytic framework for clinical utility eval-
uation, and develops statistical and computational methods for multiplex rule formulation and performance
estimation. These tools will facilitate personalized treatment and patient care for cancers and other diseases.

title: Vanderbilt Training Program in Molecular and Genetic Epidemiology of Cancer
text:
The Vanderbilt training program in Molecular and Genetic Epidemiology of Cancer is designed to build an elite
class of epidemiologists to lead the new era of multidisciplinary collaborative research in cancer. The program,
built upon an outstanding research and education training environment; excellent body of researchers and
educators; multiple, ongoing, cutting-edge research projects; exceptional data/biospecimen and population
resources; and the rich history of interdisciplinary training at Vanderbilt, delivers individualized didactic and
research training to equip postdoctoral fellows from a variety of disciplines with the methodological tools,
practical laboratory and survey-research knowledge, and hands-on research and grant writing experience
necessary to launch independent careers in the molecular and genetic epidemiology of cancer.

title: Complete human parent-of-origin genome: functional signatures and developmental determinants of disease.
text:
Only a few dozen genomic imprinting loci are well validated in humans where a handful of these cause rare
congenital disorders if the imprinting signature is disturbed. We hypothesize that human imprinting catalog is
incomplete and may lead to misassignment of true rare developmental disease alleles.

title: Design and Development of an Evidence-based Cognitive Aid for Out-of-Hospital Treatment of Pediatric Patients
text: Safety events are prevalent in prehospital pediatric care, potentially resulting in childhood morbidity and mortality. Enhancing emergency care for pediatric patients in the out-of-hospital setting is of paramount importance and holds great societal benefits, as it has the potential to significantly improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs. The objective of this research is to design, develop, and evaluate an evidence- based, context-sensitive cognitive aid to assist prehospital providers in recognizing patients' requirements and delivering timely interventions for the treatment and stabilization of pediatric patients in the field.

title: Deciphering the Glycan Code in Human Alzheimer's Disease Brain
text:
Glycosylation is an abundant and complex co-translational modification of proteins that impacts protein folding,
maturation, stability, subcellular localization, and enzymatic activity. While critical roles of N-linked
glycosylation are beginning to emerge in the brain, its involvement in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely
unknown. We provided preliminary data in support of N-linked glycan alterations as a driver of AD disease
pathology, the goal of this proposal is to define the cellular and extracellular events underlying altered N-link
glycan metabolism in AD.

title: eCD4-Mediated Control of SIV Infection in the Brain
text:
Although small-molecule antiretroviral therapy (ART) drugs effectively control an HIV infection, there are
drawbacks to their use, including their inability to prevent HIV-associated neurological disease in many
patients. We have previously shown that expression of the exceptionally broad and potent antibody-like
inhibitor eCD4, expressed from a gene-therapy vector, can protect from challenge with and often control
infection of HIV model viruses. Here, we will determine if we can apply this approach to effectively treat the
neurological consequences of HIV infection.

title: Impact of Gut Epithelial Serotonin on Afferent Neuron Function and Visceral Pain Signaling
text:
Visceral (i.e., abdominal) pain is a debilitating symptom of prevalent gastrointestinal disorders such as
irritable bowel syndrome, and current treatments are ineffective. The proposed experiments will define how
serotonin in the gut influences pain sensing neurons and investigate novel therapeutic mechanisms for visceral
pain treatment.

title: Metabolic Imaging to Enable Targeted Therapy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
text:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the most common form of liver cancer, has a five-year survival rate of just 18%,
highlighting the urgent need for better diagnostic and treatment methods. This proposal aims to develop novel,
non-invasive imaging strategies using hyperpolarized magnetic resonance imaging and positron emission
tomography to quantify tumor metabolism in real-time, offering valuable insights into tumor biology and metabolic
vulnerabilities. If successful, this research could greatly enhance treatment outcomes for HCC patients through
targeted therapies and advanced monitoring techniques.

title: A Novel Glycosaminoglycan Mimetic Scaffold for Cartilage Repair
text:
An estimated 49 million Americans, or 1 of every 6 adults, are affected by cartilage damage. Current surgical
procedures result in inadequate repair suffering from poor integration with surrounding hyaline cartilage and
the formation of fibrocartilage instead of normal hyaline cartilage. The approach described here is to combine
the surgical treatment of microfracturing, which will provide endogenous cells capable of chondrogenesis to the
defect site, with a novel scaffold that mimics the cartilage extracellular matrix during development to promote
chondrogenesis and cartilage tissue formation.

title: Targeting posttranslational modifications of CD73 in TNBCs
text:
Results from recent TCGA and pathological studies imply the oncogenic role for CD73
in breast tumor evasion and progression, although the underlying molecular mechanisms by which
dysregulation of CD73 by ubiquitin-proteasome pathway contributes to breast tumor evasion, progression
and metastasis remain unknown. This proposal will determine the impact of CD74 proteolytic regulation
by TRIM21 in breast carcinogenesis, and further determine the clinical relevance of modulation of CD73
turnover regulation in anti-breast cancer treatment, especially for triple negative type breast cancers.
Completion of this project will uncover the molecular underling of CD73 ubiquitination by TRIM21 in breast
carcinogenesis and tumor microenvironment, and could provide a new strategy for breast cancer therapy
by targeting TRIM21-CD73 axis.

title: Probing real-time conformational dynamics and allosteric cooperativity of the HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein during virus entry
text:
The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) enters host cells that fight infection and uses those cells to reproduce
itself, causing infected people to become vulnerable to other infections and diseases. Structural dynamics of the
HIV surface protein envelope promotes HIV entering susceptible cells via membrane fusion and helps the virus
evade antibodies. This research will provide valuable new insights into the time-resolved structural dynamics
and allostery of the HIV envelope to better inform the design of envelope-centric interventions such as vaccines,
antibody therapy, and anti-viral drugs.

title: Development and Validation of a Compliant Reversible Actuator and Detector Leveraging Electrophysiology for Organoids (Organoid-CRADLE)
text:
Neural organoids are small clusters of human-origin brain cells that can help scientists develop new medicines
and understand the brain. Unfortunately, measuring and manipulating their function is difficult. We plan to
develop a new tool for this purpose that will be more versatile, more informative, and less injurious than current
options.

title: Core B: Human and Clinical Phenotyping Core
text: CORE B Core B has the overarching goal of supporting the Scientific Projects by providing reliable and readily available clinical data from patients and will support the Project Investigators by collecting, processing, and analyzing a rich multi-omics dataset from patients undergoing lung transplantation. Investigators in the Core will collect detailed clinical data from lung transplant recipients and manually adjudicate clinical episodes and the diagnosis of PGD and CLAD. Core B investigators will identify clinical and research procedures that will generate biologic material and enroll patients in observational studies. Core B will work synergistically with the Core C investigators to process the samples to generate single cell suspensions that will be analyzed using flow cytometry and single cell RNA-sequencing/CITE seq, paired fixed tissue for spatial transcriptomics, and other assays. Core B will apply robust machine learning approaches to organize clinical data and use this framework as a scaffold to overlay longitudinally collected genomic and proteomic data collected over the clinical course of transplantation. The resulting models of clinical PGD and CLAD will be used to identify biomarkers and generate hypotheses about biologic pathways that will be causally tested in the Projects, credentialling the pathways as therapeutic targets. Hence, Core B will directly support the Projects through the following aims. Aim 1. To enroll lung transplant recipients for prospective tissue collection and data integration throughout longitudinal care. We have developed integrated clinical and research teams to enable patient enrollment and collection of events over the clinical course of patients. The clinical data extracted from the electronic health record will complement the molecular phenotyping data and enable the Scientific Projects to test the hypotheses outlined. This integrated model will facilitate the identification of biomarkers and clinical predictors of transitions in clinical state after transplantation. Aim 2. To process, immunophenotype, and cryopreserve biological material from the lung and esophagus collected as part of clinical care or research. We will leverage our experience with sample collection, processing, flow cytometry, single cell RNA-sequencing, metabolomic and spatial transcriptomic profiling to develop a robust multi-omics dataset of patients undergoing lung transplantation. Aim 3. To perform next-generation sequencing assays, including single-cell RNA-seq, CITE-seq, and single cell TCR and BCR clonotyping as well as spatial transcriptomics on selected samples. A major challenge in data science has been the integration of large-scale datasets coming from multiple groups. Through collaborations with the Chan Zuckerberg Human Cell Atlas Consortium, we have contributed to approaches based on transfer learning that allow integration of single cell transcriptomic data rapidly and at scale. We will apply these approaches to the multi-omics data collected from our patients to inform analyses proposed by the Project Investigators.

title: Validation of the molecular origin of APT-Weighted Imaging in tumors
text:
Variations in membrane lipid content are frequently seen as sensitive indicators of abnormal cellular processes
associated with many diseases, such as tumors. An MRI technique that can non-invasively map membrane
lipids in vivo would hold significant diagnostic potential and provide a novel biomarker for pathological
changes. The proposed research aims to redefine APTw MR imaging as a lipid imaging technique is of great
importance for healthcare.

title: Liver-Sparing APOE Inhibitor for the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease in APOE4 Homozygotes
text:
Switch Therapeutics is developing a novel RNAi therapeutic to knock down APOE and localize this effect to the
CNS for the treatment of Alzheimer's Disease in APOE4 homozygous patients. The goal of this project is to
better understand the expected biomarker readouts in relation to target knockdown and duration to inform the
clinical biomarker strategy, develop assays to better characterize the tissue PK/metabolism and PD, and to run
a dose-range finding study to inform IND-enabling safety studies. If successful, this novel therapeutic strategy
targeting APOE will enable treatment options for a subset of AD patients carrying two copies of the APOE4
gene.

title: Nanopore Sequencing for Pediatric Central Nervous System Tumor Classification
text:
Central nervous system tumors are the leading cause of pediatric cancer-related deaths, and
optimal outcomes for patients are heavily reliant on accurate DNA methylation-based diagnoses. Nanopore
sequencing of native DNA provides a fast and comprehensive option for this information, but there are still
large gaps in machine-learning based diagnosis of exclusively pediatric central nervous system tumors, as
the tumor entities are much different than those of adults and the tumor microenvironments are typically
heavily composed of non-tumor tissues. This proposal centers a project around children and adolescent
tumors and leverages the unique qualities of long-read sequencing to develop machine learning methods
for resolving age-related biological differences and clustering methods for resolving tumor heterogeneity, all
in the ultimate pursuit of extending survival for pediatric patients with central nervous system tumors.

title: Redox and Proteomic Stress Responses in Biliary Disease
text:
Diseases of the bile ducts are an important cause of liver failure in the adult and pediatric populations. We have
discovered differences in the way bile duct cells respond to environmental stress and will examine the underlying
causes and their relevance to human biliary diseases.

title: Lipid-mediated fungal pathogenesis
text:
Fungal infections have dramatically increased during the last decade and new treatment options are needed. This proposal
focuses on the characterization of new fungal vaccines and new antifungal compounds, providing new insights into the
development of better therapeutic strategies.

title: Bionic Self-Charged Bone Composite Scaffold
text:
Reconstruction of large and major bone defects remains a significant challenge in orthopedic surgery. Yet, the
golden treatments so far, using replacement auto or allo-grafts, struggle with many problems of immune
rejection, infection, donor-site morbidity and especially, limited tissue supplies. Here, we propose a new
approach to combine special biodegradable piezoelectric Poly-l-Lactide (PLLA) nanofibers with Tricalcium
Phosphate (β-TCP) to create a bionic bone composite scaffold which can be activated by ultrasound (US) to
electrically stimulate a complete healing of critical-sized bone defects in vivo.

title: Targeting disulfidptosis in cancer: mechanisms and preclinical translation
text:
In contrast to our deep understanding of other cell death modalities such as apoptosis and ferroptosis,
the molecular underpinnings of disulfidptosis (a newly discovered cell death that is induced by disulfide stress),
along with its therapeutic implications, remain largely unexplored. The objectives of this application are to
elucidate the mechanisms underlying disulfidptosis and to therapeutically target this form of cell death in
SLC7A11-high cancers. Our proposed studies will have significant impact on both our understanding of the
fundamental mechanisms of disulfidptosis and our ability to target this cell death pathway in cancer treatment.
